text:
Predicates:
RankedHigh(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is among the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
RolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated at Roland Garros 2022.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.
Player(x) ::: x is a player.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHigh(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If a player is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are among the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, i) → RankedHigh(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (FemalePlayer(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x) → LostTo(x, i)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
(∀x (FemalePlayer(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x))) ∨ (∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x))) ::: Either female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 or male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ RolandGarros2022(x) → LostTo(x, r)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
∀x ((CocoGauff(x) ∧ (RankedHigh(x) ∨ LostTo(x, r))) → ¬MalePlayer(x)) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player.

Conclusion:
LostTo(cocoGauff, r) ::: Coco Gauff has lost to Rafael Nadal.
